findings.message: Change 041 is a delivery-module change, but this round edits platform code: packages/core/src/env.ts (AMAX_TODAY, clockFromEnv), packages/core/src/service.ts (Runtime.now, now()), packages/core/src/server.ts (the export) and apps/web/lib/server.ts (the wiring). The module standard says a module change touches only modules/<name>/ plus one CODEOWNERS line, and the architecture says the platform team owns packages/ and apps/web. Fix: move the core clock adapter and its web wiring into its own platform-lane change, and have 041 depend on it. 041 then only calls now() from @amax/core/server.
findings.scenario: The 041 diff changes 4 files outside modules/delivery/ → the module-standard check 'the change touches only modules/<name>/' fails, and a platform-owned contract (Runtime) changes without platform review.

findings.message: Instance fix of 'a released proposal with no release'. Only CON-009 got a real release. HRI-104 'Login hotfix' is still seeded as phase 'released' with releasedAt 2026-10-06 and no release. It has no Prod deployment behind it, yet shippedPerWeek counts it as shipped to Prod in W41 and the CSV shows Release '' and Shipped to 'Prod'. The new test only checks the CON project's released proposals, so this variant is never tested. Fix: link HRI-104 to a real HRI release (for example a v0.9.2 hotfix release with a deployed Prod stage), and make the test assert that every released proposal in every project has a release.
findings.scenario: listProposals(maya, { projectKey: 'HRI', phase: 'released' }) → HRI-104 has release null, yet shippedPerWeek W41 = 1 counts it as shipped to Prod.

findings.message: onActiveMap decides 'superseded' by the release row's createdAt (when the row was inserted), not by which release is newer in deployment order. A release recorded later can therefore hide the one that is actually current: a backfilled older version, or one imported by specclaw sync. Fix: treat a Live release as superseded only by a same-project release whose first deployment is later than this release's Prod deployment (or compare by version order). Add a test case where the older release has the later createdAt.
findings.scenario: FLT v1.8.0 is live in Prod since Oct 10. A PM then backfills FLT v1.7.2, which has a UAT deployment, so v1.7.2 gets the later createdAt → v1.8.0 counts as superseded and drops off the Active map, while v1.7.2 stays on it.

findings.message: The 'missing week is null' fix only handles the case where every week is missing. In that case ProjectsPage shows its empty state. When only some weeks are missing, LineChart drops the null points and then runs `curve(pts)` and the area fill straight across the gap. The chart then shows a smooth line and shaded area through a week that has no roll-up, so it looks like real data. Only the screen-reader table says 'No data'. Fix: break the path into one segment per run of consecutive non-null points, and do the same for the area. Never interpolate across a null. Add a variant test with a null in the middle, a null at the start and a null at the end.
findings.scenario: Ingestion writes the W40 and W42 portfolio rows but not W41. weeklyThroughput returns done [..., 35, null, 38]. The chart draws a continuous curve from 35 to 38 through W41, so W41 looks like it had about 36 tasks done.

findings.message: The new 4% allowance uses the selector `.cols.even > .card`, which matches both cards in that row: the phase card and the shipped chart. The tolerance meant for the shipped chart therefore also hides regressions in the phase card. Fix: narrow the selector to the shipped chart's card.
findings.scenario: A 3% pixel regression in the phase-legend card on /delivery/proposals → the visual test still passes.

findings.message: Shipped-to-Prod demo data now differs from fixtures.md's W35–W42 series [2,3,1,4,3,5,4,6]: the app shows W41 = 1 and W42 = 0. The reason is recorded only in the visual-test allowance. Fix: record the decision in .specclaw/changes/001-amax-foundation/fixtures.md (or a note in the module README), so the fixtures stay 'consistent with fixtures.md'.
findings.scenario: fixtures.md says W42 = 6 shipped → the app's chart shows 0.

findings.message: Migration 0009 is edited in place to drop the `shipped` column, not changed by a follow-up migration. If 0009 has already run on any dev or preview database, that database keeps the old column, and a checksum-verifying runner would reject the edited file. This is fine only if 0009 has never been applied outside this branch. Otherwise add a 0010 that drops the column.

Three problems with the new tests. (1) The weekly-charts test inserts a CON per-project weekly_stat row into the shared seeded tenant and never removes it, so later tests and visual runs against the same database see changed data. Run it in a rolled-back transaction or delete the row afterwards. (2) The 'a tenant with none at all' assertion actually queries the same tenant at a far-future date, so it does not cover a tenant with no data. (3) clock.test.ts calls configureRuntime with a fake db and never resets it, so the fake runtime leaks to other tests in the same worker.
